source.title: The instabilities of large learning rate training: a loss landscape view

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure references are malformed (for example, “Fig. ??”), and plotted values are not provided numerically.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies gradient-descent instability at large learning rates and reports loss and Hessian behavior, using cross-entropy classification experiments rather than the squared-loss wide-network setup in V5.
record.gate_note: Results concern large-learning-rate training dynamics and loss-landscape behavior. The paper does not report training classification error, so it does not test V1. CIFAR-10 results include figures and textual descriptions but no exact plotted values. References to results from Cohen et al. and Lewkowycz et al. are prior work, not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own full-batch gradient-descent loss and curvature dynamics above the stability limit, bearing on V5's non-divergent instability component using cross-entropy classification. It does not establish the complete squared-loss catapult sequence or sustained low training loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors characterize non-divergent instability phases, associate repeated instabilities with reduced solution sharpness, and report learning-rate-dependent landscape shifts. They caution that large non-divergent rates need not guarantee consistent long-timescale objective decrease; this caution is not itself a measured failure of training-loss recovery.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient descent with cross-entropy classification experiments on FMNIST and CIFAR-10; it does not reproduce the squared-loss wide-network learning-rate experiments described in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes landscape similarity: higher η makes similarity windows more local and trajectories less similar to the η = 0.01 baseline. In the cyclic-schedule experiment, different η+ and η− choices lead to different Hessian movements; the ηhigh = 0.30, ηlow = 0.05 schedule diverges.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-10 validation loss and approximate Hessian measures display corresponding instability phases after epoch 700.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-learning-rate classification training can produce coordinated fluctuations in validation loss and curvature measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Delaying learning-rate reduction generally lowers worst-case solution sharpness, with late increases at η = 0.25 and 0.30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The timing of learning-rate reduction affects subsequent solution sharpness.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing the learning rate makes Hessian-subspace similarity more local and trajectories less similar to the smooth baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large learning rates alter the orientation of the explored loss landscape.

record.peer_reviewed: HLD 2023: 1st Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics
record.problems: The central CIFAR-10 trajectory is a specific run and relies on an approximate Hessian; the authors note they could not compute S(v) because of GPU memory limits. Several outcomes are described through figures without numerical values. The experiments use small benchmarks and do not report training classification error.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and model-size or regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies, and the effect of additional student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization, or Fixup.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.

The wide-network squared-loss catapult sequence ending in low training loss; quantitative comparison with the initial linearized stability limit; sharpness hovering at 2/η while training loss falls over long times; and divergence despite initialization below the threshold. Appendix D uses MSE for synthetic regression, but its reported perturbation experiments do not establish these dynamics.
Batch-normalization comparisons and normalization-free Fixup training speed or stability.

missing.what: The cyclic schedule ηhigh = 0.30, ηlow = 0.05 diverges. Record the schedule: 10 epochs at the upper rate, 50 at the lower rate, repeated, with the final 40 epochs at the lower rate. Do not infer an exact divergence threshold from this comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Remove the extracted limits_scope labels: missing evidence of low training loss does not demonstrate a limitation of V5. The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted values, so numerical loss levels and threshold tracking cannot be reconstructed.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, including on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 and with corrupted or random labels, is not reported.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or bad-local-minimum outcomes are tested.
No depth comparison of plain and residual networks is reported.
No initialization comparison or initialization-dependent trainable-depth result is reported.

The study examines large-learning-rate instability and curvature in classification networks, but does not test squared loss, wide networks, or the stated stability-limit recipe. No numerical training-loss outcomes are reported; figure-based loss behavior is described only in general terms.
Batch normalization and its effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance are not tested.

rows.subject: 5-layer MLP with 32 hidden units in each layer
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent training at large learning rates on FMNIST; the paper describes spikes during unstable training followed by metric recovery.

conditions.value: FMNIST; first 4 classes; training set b = 1000
unstable regime; particular trajectory’s unstable regime begins at η = 0.03

rows.measure: Training trajectory and loss-landscape metrics during instability
rows.baseline: Pre-spike values in the same trajectory
rows.value: Instability spikes are non-divergent; model metrics return to pre-spike values.
rows.note: The description reports recovery from spikes but does not give numerical loss values or establish that training loss becomes low.
rows.check: Observed for transient instability and recovery: Section 3 explicitly reports non-divergent spikes with metrics returning to pre-spike values. Low final training loss is unestablished, rather than demonstrated incomplete recovery. The η = 0.03 boundary is stated for the particular initialization in Figure 3; its applicability to Figure 1 is not explicitly established.

rows.subject: modified AlexNet
rows.size_stated: Convolution layers: 64 features with (5, 5) kernels and (2, 2) strides; dense layers with 382 and 196 hidden units
rows.operation_detail: Training trajectory at η = 0.06; Hessian measures computed with a k-layer approximation.
rows.measure: Training trajectory, validation loss, SANE Neff, and λmax
rows.value: The trajectory displays phases of instability after epoch 700; loss and the measures show corresponding peaks and troughs.
rows.note: The text does not report numerical training-loss values or say that training loss reaches a low value. The Hessian calculation is an approximation; the paper says the output-layer-only computation differs significantly from k = 2, 3.
rows.check: Figure 7 plots validation loss and approximate Hessian measures. Calling this a training trajectory does not make its loss measure training loss. Neither recovery of the training objective nor sharpness relative to 2/η is established. Add the 5,000-example training subset to the condition.

rows.subject: 5-layer MLP with 32 hidden units in each layer
rows.operation_detail: Training at large learning rates with the timing of learning-rate reduction varied; the paper compares worst-case solution sharpness.

conditions.value: η reduction timing varied; figures discuss η = 0.25 and η = 0.30

rows.measure: Worst-case maximum Hessian eigenvalue of solutions
rows.baseline: Smooth trajectory; η reduction to equal the benchmark smooth trajectory
rows.value: On large timescales, worst-case λmax decreases as η reduction is delayed; the final few data points for η = 0.25 and η = 0.30 show an increase.
rows.note: This reports a curvature trend, not the loss rise and recovery pattern or low training loss specified in V5.
rows.check: This measures solution sharpness after reducing the learning rate at different times. It does not measure curvature dropping during loss recovery, sharpness hovering at the stability threshold, or training-loss improvement. The reported trend is valid but does not establish a V5 outcome.

relationships.condition: Full-batch FMNIST cross-entropy training in the unstable learning-rate regime; transient recovery component
relationships.reason: R1 reports loss spikes followed by recovery to pre-spike metric values, supporting non-divergent instability; sustained low training loss remains untested.
relationships.display_finding: Loss spikes were followed by recovery to pre-spike metric values.

relationships.condition: Cyclic learning rates with ηhigh = 0.30 and ηlow = 0.05
relationships.reason: Appendix E.1, Figure 11 explicitly reports divergence for this schedule, supporting the possibility of divergence at large rates; this result is missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: The cyclic schedule with ηhigh = 0.30 and ηlow = 0.05 diverged.
